study type: Secondary analysis of a cross-sectional study
exposure: Use of antibiotic prophylaxis for caesarean section
Timing of caesarean section (before or after labor)
Indication for caesarean section (scheduled or emergency)
outcome: Coverage of antibiotic prophylaxis for caesarean section
cohort: Data from 359 health facilities with the capacity to perform caesarean section in 29 countries participating in the World Health Organization Multicountry Survey on Maternal and Newborn Health
finding: Coverage of antibiotic prophylaxis for caesarean birth varied greatly between countries and was related to guideline use and the practice of clinical audits, but not to the size, location of the institution or development index of the country.
mod_finding: Mothers with complications and those undergoing scheduled caesarean births were more likely to receive antibiotic prophylaxis, despite their lower risk of infection compared with mothers undergoing emergency caesarean section.
